title:
Same model.
Better loop.
benefit: A notebook gets you a number. A workspace gets you evidence.
lines: Let's train a house price model the way most of us do: in a notebook, in Colab or VS Code. Then in AI Engineering IDE.
Same data, same scikit-learn code. The difference is everything around the code.

title:
Results live
in cell output.
benefit: Re-run a cell and the last result is gone.
lines: In a notebook, you run a cell and read the score it prints.
Change a hyperparameter and run it again, and the previous result is overwritten, unless you copied it somewhere.
Comparing runs, keeping track of saved models, and remembering what changed is left to you, or to an extra tool like MLflow or Weights and Biases.

title:
Start from
a checklist.
benefit: Home shows what is set up and what to do next.
lines: Here, the project opens on Home. The Train a model card tracks what is already set up.
The training command is configured and the environment is installed. The next step is to start a training job.

captions.text: Here, the project opens on Home. The Train a model card tracks what is already set up.

title:
Watch it
learn.
benefit: Learning curves stream in while the job runs.
lines: In Training, choose the train command and set the parameters: two hundred trees, a learning rate of zero point one, and depth three.
Start training. Training and validation error stream in while the job runs, instead of appearing only after the cell finishes.
It finishes with a validation R squared of zero point nine zero, and the trained model is recorded as an artifact.

title:
Compare,
don't guess.
benefit: Overlay a new run on the baseline and spot overfitting as it happens.
lines: Now try a bigger model: three hundred trees, depth eight, and a learning rate of zero point two.
Select the baseline as the comparison run. Its curves appear dashed, on the same charts.
Training error falls far lower, but validation error starts climbing after about thirty trees. That is overfitting, visible while it happens.
The final validation R squared drops to zero point eight eight, so the baseline stays.

title:
Every run,
remembered.
benefit: Parameters, metrics, and evaluations saved for every experiment.
lines: In Runs, both experiments are saved with their exact parameters, duration, metrics, and evaluation results.
They are still there after restarting the IDE, and you can compare any two side by side.

captions.text: In Runs, both experiments are saved with their exact parameters, duration, metrics, and evaluation results.

title:
Every step,
timed.
benefit: From a slow or failing step straight to its code.
lines: The trace breaks each run into steps: load the data, split it, fit, evaluate, and save.
Select a step to see its timing and attributes, or jump straight to the code that produced it.

title:
The model,
not a mystery file.
benefit: Saved models stay linked to the run that made them.
lines: Back in Training, the saved model is linked to the run that created it.
Inspect it to find the exact file, ready to load for inference.

title:
Less bookkeeping.
More evidence.
benefit: Plain Python code. The IDE keeps the record.
lines: Notebooks are great for quick exploration, and Colab gives you free hosted GPUs.
For iterating on a model, this workspace records every run, charts it live, compares experiments, and keeps models traceable, without setting up a separate tracking server.
Your code stays plain Python with a few logging calls. The IDE keeps the record.
